reason: B ships a working, keyboard-accessible, clearly labelled swap demo and limits simulator: no console errors, axe clean, no overflow down to 320, a working mobile menu, and a no-JS fallback. A is a tidy static page whose artifacts are pictures, with inert look-alike buttons, unlabelled sample data, 8 contrast failures and a clipped headline at 320. What would change my mind: if B's script state bugs corrupted the roster under some input sequence, but every sequence I tried rendered consistent state.
